note: Curated by Cosmic Library. URLs verified against web search on 2026-09-26. Organisation names appear as text chips only; no logos.

entries.title: NASA Systems Engineering Handbook (SP-2016-6105 Rev 2)
entries.description: The agency's own playbook for turning a mission idea into flight hardware: life-cycle phases, technical reviews, requirements, verification and validation. If you read one engineering document on this page, read this one.

entries.title: Basics of Space Flight
entries.description: JPL's classic self-paced primer, originally written to train mission operations staff. It walks from the Solar System and gravity through interplanetary trajectories, spacecraft subsystems and the Deep Space Network, with quizzes along the way.

entries.title: Beginner's Guide to Rockets
entries.description: Hundreds of short illustrated pages from NASA Glenn Research Center on thrust, drag, stability, nozzles and the rocket equation. Each page is one idea and one equation, perfect for building intuition before a textbook.

entries.title: Rockets Educator Guide
entries.description: Classroom-tested activities from straw rockets to water rockets, each tied to Newton's laws of motion. A ready-made lab manual for anyone who teaches, or wants to learn by building.

entries.title: Space Launch System (SLS) Reference Guide
entries.description: NASA's illustrated guide to the Space Launch System (SLS): stage-by-stage anatomy, RS-25 engines, solid rocket boosters and Artemis mission profiles. Excellent cutaway art and hard numbers in one place.

entries.title: Artemis Plan: NASA's Lunar Exploration Program Overview
entries.description: The 2020 architecture document that explains how Orion, the Space Launch System (SLS), Gateway and commercial landers fit together to return people to the Moon. Read it to see how an agency explains a campaign, not just a mission.

entries.title: Human Spaceflight Standards and the Human Integration Design Handbook (HIDH)
entries.source: NASA Office of the Chief Health & Medical Officer
entries.description: NASA's hub for human-system standards and the Human Integration Design Handbook (HIDH), the companion that turns them into design data: reach envelopes, acoustics, lighting, vibration, cabin atmosphere. The reference for designing anything a crew touches.

entries.title: NASA-STD-3001 Space Flight Human-System Standard, Volume 1: Crew Health
entries.description: The binding standard that sets how much radiation, g-load, noise and isolation a crew may be exposed to. Volume 2 covers human factors and habitability; together they drive every crewed vehicle's requirements.

entries.title: NASA Technical Standards System
entries.source: NASA Office of the Chief Engineer
entries.description: The searchable library of agency-wide engineering standards, from fracture control and fastener design to software assurance. See how 'good engineering' gets written down as a requirement.

entries.title: Technology Readiness Levels (TRL)
entries.description: The nine-step scale NASA invented to answer 'how ready is this technology?', from basic principles observed (TRL 1) to flight proven (TRL 9). Now used across aerospace, defence and research funding worldwide.

entries.title: NASA Lessons Learned Information System (LLIS)
entries.source: NASA Office of the Chief Engineer
entries.description: Thousands of short write-ups of what went wrong (and right) on real projects, each with a driving event, lesson and recommendation. Reading ten of these is a crash course in engineering judgement.

entries.title: State-of-the-Art of Small Spacecraft Technology
entries.source: NASA Ames Small Spacecraft Systems Virtual Institute
entries.description: A regularly updated survey of what small-satellite hardware can actually do today: power, propulsion, attitude control, communications, avionics and more, subsystem by subsystem. The fastest way to sanity-check a CubeSat design.

entries.title: CubeSat 101: Basic Concepts and Processes for First-Time CubeSat Developers
entries.description: A plain-English walk through a first CubeSat project: team building, design, licensing, testing and getting a ride to orbit through the CubeSat Launch Initiative (CSLI). Written for university teams.

entries.title: Apollo Flight Journal
entries.description: Annotated, minute-by-minute air-to-ground transcripts of the Apollo missions in flight, with commentary explaining every burn, checklist and callout. The best way to feel how a lunar mission was flown.

entries.title: Apollo Lunar Surface Journal
entries.description: The companion to the Flight Journal for time on the Moon: every moonwalk transcript annotated by the astronauts themselves, plus photos, equipment documents and press kits.

entries.title: Saturn V Flight Manual SA-503
entries.description: The crew-training description of the Saturn V that flew Apollo 8: stage systems, F-1 and J-2 engines, instrument unit, flight sequence and abort modes. Primary-source rocket engineering at its finest.

entries.title: Saturn V Launch Vehicle Flight Evaluation Report AS-506 (Apollo 11)
entries.description: How the Moon rocket actually performed on Apollo 11: measured thrust, trajectory, vibration and every anomaly, compared against prediction. This is what post-flight engineering looks like.

entries.title: Apollo 11 Press Kit
entries.description: The briefing NASA handed reporters in June 1969: mission timeline, landing site, experiments, spacecraft and crew. Clear, confident and full of numbers.

entries.title: Apollo 11 Mission Report
entries.description: The official post-flight analysis of the first landing, including the famous 1201/1202 computer alarms, fuel margins at touchdown and each spacecraft system's performance.

entries.title: Apollo Program Summary Report (JSC-09423)
entries.description: One volume covering the whole Apollo program: every flight, every spacecraft system, science results and program management. The best single-document overview of how Apollo was engineered.

entries.title: Stages to Saturn (NASA SP-4206)
entries.description: Roger Bilstein's technological history of the Saturn rockets, free online: how the F-1 combustion instability was tamed, how liquid hydrogen was mastered, and how a nation built a Moon rocket.

entries.title: Space Shuttle News Reference Manual (1988)
entries.description: A system-by-system tour of the Space Shuttle written for journalists but detailed enough for engineers: orbiter structures, thermal protection, main engines, boosters, avionics and mission operations.

entries.title: Report of the Presidential Commission on the Space Shuttle Challenger Accident
entries.description: The investigation of the 1986 Challenger loss, including Richard Feynman's appendix on reliability. Required reading on how technical warnings get lost inside organisations.

entries.title: Columbia Accident Investigation Board (CAIB) Report, Volume 1
entries.description: The Columbia Accident Investigation Board (CAIB) traced the 2003 loss to foam striking the wing's leading edge, then went further to diagnose the organisational causes. A masterclass in failure analysis.

entries.title: Mars 2020 Perseverance Landing Press Kit
entries.description: The web press kit for Perseverance's 2021 landing: entry, descent and landing step by step, the sky crane, the rover's instruments and the Ingenuity helicopter. Beautifully clear.

entries.title: NASA Technical Reports Server (NTRS)
entries.source: NASA Scientific and Technical Information Program
entries.description: Over half a million NASA technical reports, papers and memos, most free to download. If you want the original analysis behind almost any NASA vehicle, it is probably in here.

entries.title: NASA Space Science Data Coordinated Archive (NSSDCA)
entries.description: NASA's permanent archive of space science data, with a catalog entry for nearly every spacecraft ever launched and the much-loved planetary fact sheets.

entries.title: Planetary Data System (PDS)
entries.description: The official, peer-reviewed archive for every NASA planetary mission's data: raw and calibrated images, spectra and telemetry from Voyager to Perseverance.

entries.title: NASA Exoplanet Archive
entries.description: The authoritative table of confirmed planets beyond the Solar System, with orbital and stellar parameters you can plot or download. Great for data-science projects.

entries.title: NASA Image and Video Library
entries.description: Over 140,000 searchable NASA photos, videos and audio files, most of them public domain. Where the imagery on this site comes from.

entries.title: NASA's Eyes on the Solar System
entries.description: A browser-based 3D model of the Solar System driven by real JPL trajectory data. Ride along with any active spacecraft, now or at any date in its mission.

entries.title: JPL Horizons On-Line Ephemeris System
entries.description: Precise positions and velocities of more than a million Solar System bodies and many spacecraft, via web app, email, telnet or Application Programming Interface (API). The same ephemerides JPL navigators use.

entries.title: JPL Small-Body Database
entries.description: Orbital elements, physical data and orbit diagrams for every known asteroid and comet, with an API behind it. Look up any rock and see its orbit in 3D.

entries.title: NAIF SPICE Toolkit
entries.source: JPL Navigation and Ancillary Information Facility (NAIF)
entries.description: The toolkit planetary missions use to answer geometry questions: where was the spacecraft, which way was the camera pointing, when does the Sun set at the landing site. Free in C, Fortran, MATLAB and Interactive Data Language (IDL), with excellent tutorials.

entries.title: General Mission Analysis Tool (GMAT)
entries.description: NASA's open-source, flight-qualified tool for designing and optimising trajectories from low Earth orbit (LEO) to libration points and deep space. Used operationally on real missions.

entries.title: Chemical Equilibrium with Applications (CEA)
entries.description: The standard code for predicting combustion temperature, exhaust composition and theoretical specific impulse of any propellant combination. Behind countless engine trade studies since the 1960s.

entries.title: NASA Software Catalog
entries.description: Over a thousand NASA-developed programs available to the public, from trajectory tools and structural analysis to autonomy and data processing, organised by category.

entries.title: NASA Open Source Software (code.nasa.gov)
entries.description: The directory of NASA's openly licensed code, from flight software to data tools, most of it on GitHub. Browse to see how the agency actually writes software.

entries.title: core Flight System (cFS)
entries.description: The reusable flight-software framework flown on many NASA spacecraft: a core executive, operating-system abstraction and plug-in applications. Read it to learn flight software architecture.

entries.title: F Prime (F´) Flight Software Framework
entries.description: JPL's component-based C++ framework for small spacecraft and instruments, the software that flew the Ingenuity Mars helicopter. Comes with tutorials that run on a Raspberry Pi.

entries.title: Open MCT (Open Mission Control Technologies)
entries.description: A web framework for building mission-control displays of live and historical telemetry, used by NASA missions and easy to point at your own rocket or rover.

entries.title: Orbital Debris Quarterly News
entries.description: NASA's newsletter on the orbital-debris environment since 1996: breakup events, reentries, modelling and mitigation research, with clear charts of the catalogued population.

entries.title: DSN Telecommunications Link Design Handbook (810-005)
entries.description: The Deep Space Network's (DSN) interface handbook for mission designers: antenna gains, system noise temperatures, frequencies and modulation. Everything you need to close a real deep-space link budget.

entries.title: DESCANSO Deep Space Communications and Navigation Series
entries.description: A free series of JPL monographs on radiometric navigation, the DSN's large antennas, low-noise receivers, optical communications and more, plus design summaries of real spacecraft telecom systems.

entries.title: Falcon Payload User's Guide
entries.description: What SpaceX tells satellite builders: fairing dimensions, loads, acoustic and shock environments, separation systems and launch-site services for Falcon 9 and Falcon Heavy.

entries.title: Starship Vehicle Overview
entries.description: SpaceX's official page for Starship and Super Heavy: dimensions, Raptor engines, capability and flight updates. SpaceX's 2020 Starship Users Guide (v1) outlined payload accommodations for the same vehicle.

entries.title: Atlas V Launch Services User's Guide
entries.description: One of the most detailed public launch-vehicle manuals: performance curves for every configuration, the Centaur upper stage, coupled-loads and mission integration flow.

entries.title: Vulcan Launch Systems User's Guide
entries.description: The payload planner's guide to ULA's Vulcan, successor to Atlas V: configurations, performance, fairings and environments.

entries.title: Electron Payload User's Guide
entries.description: How a dedicated small-satellite launcher works for its customers: performance to sun-synchronous orbit, the kick stage, environments and a very compressed launch campaign.

entries.title: New Glenn Payload User's Guide
entries.description: Blue Origin's guide for flying on New Glenn: the 7-metre fairing, performance, environments and the reusable first stage.

entries.title: Ariane 6 User's Manual (Issue 2)
entries.description: Europe's heavy launcher described for customers: Ariane 62 and 64 configurations, the restartable Vinci upper stage, the Guiana Space Centre and mission analysis.

entries.title: Epsilon Launch Vehicle User's Manual
entries.description: The Japan Aerospace Exploration Agency (JAXA) guide to its all-solid small launcher, notable for its highly automated, 'mobile' launch control that cut launch crews to a handful of people.

entries.title: ESA Space Environment Report 2025
entries.source: European Space Agency (ESA) Space Debris Office
entries.description: The European Space Agency's (ESA) annual health check of Earth orbit: how many objects, where, how fast the population grows, and whether operators are following the disposal rules.

entries.title: ESA Gaia Archive
entries.description: Positions, distances and motions for nearly two billion stars from ESA's Gaia mission, queryable in the browser. The most precise 3D map of our Galaxy ever made.

entries.title: ECSS Space Engineering Standards
entries.description: The European Cooperation for Space Standardization (ECSS) standards used on every ESA project, covering engineering, product assurance and project management. Free to download after registration.

entries.title: JWST User Documentation (JDox)
entries.description: Everything an astronomer needs to plan James Webb Space Telescope (JWST) observations: observatory, optics, the four science instruments, detectors and data pipelines. A superb look inside a flagship observatory.

entries.title: Hubble Space Telescope User Documentation (HDox)
entries.description: Instrument and data handbooks for the Hubble Space Telescope (HST): cameras, spectrographs, calibration and pointing. Three decades of on-orbit operations experience, written down.

entries.title: Mikulski Archive for Space Telescopes (MAST)
entries.description: The public archive for Hubble, Webb, Kepler, the Transiting Exoplanet Survey Satellite (TESS) and more. Download the same images and spectra professional astronomers use.

entries.title: 16.07 Dynamics (MIT OpenCourseWare)
entries.description: MIT's aerospace dynamics course with complete lecture notes: particle and rigid-body dynamics, central-force motion and orbits. The mathematical backbone of flight mechanics.

entries.title: 16.50 Introduction to Propulsion Systems (MIT OpenCourseWare)
entries.description: Lecture notes covering rocket and jet propulsion from first principles: nozzle flow, combustion, liquid and solid rockets, and electric propulsion.

entries.title: 16.346 Astrodynamics (MIT OpenCourseWare)
entries.description: Graduate astrodynamics in the tradition of Richard Battin, who designed Apollo's guidance equations: two-body problem, Lambert's problem, perturbations and navigation.

entries.title: 16.851 Satellite Engineering (MIT OpenCourseWare)
entries.description: Graduate course on designing satellites subsystem by subsystem: orbits, power, thermal, attitude control, communications and structures, tied together by design projects.

entries.title: CelesTrak
entries.description: Free orbital element sets for every tracked satellite, plus classic tutorial columns on coordinate systems and the two-line element (TLE) format.

entries.title: General Catalog of Artificial Space Objects (GCAT)
entries.description: Astrophysicist Jonathan McDowell's meticulous catalog of every launch and every object sent to space, the go-to dataset for spaceflight statistics.

entries.title: Rocket & Space Technology
entries.description: A long-running engineer's site with worked numerical examples for orbital mechanics, rocket propulsion and atmospheric models. Great for checking your own calculations.

entries.title: OpenRocket
entries.description: The free, open-source model-rocket designer and six-degree-of-freedom flight simulator. Draw a rocket, pick a motor, check stability and predict apogee before you build.

entries.title: poliastro
entries.description: An approachable Python library for orbital mechanics: propagate orbits, plan Hohmann transfers, solve Lambert's problem and plot it all. The original project is archived; the hapsira fork continues it.

entries.title: Orekit
entries.description: A professional-grade open-source flight dynamics library (Java, with Python wrappers) for propagation, orbit determination, maneuvers and attitude, used in operational ground systems.

entries.title: Basilisk Astrodynamics Simulation Framework
entries.source: Autonomous Vehicle Systems (AVS) Lab, University of Colorado Boulder
entries.description: A fast, modular spacecraft simulation framework (C/C++ core, Python scripting) for attitude dynamics, control and flight-software testing, used in research and real missions.

entries.title: Skyfield
entries.description: Elegant Python for positional astronomy: where is Mars tonight, when does the International Space Station (ISS) pass overhead, when is sunrise. Uses JPL ephemerides under the hood.

entries.title: Astropy
entries.description: The community-built core Python package for astronomy: units, time scales, coordinate frames, FITS files and tables. Almost every modern astronomy notebook imports it.

entries.title: CubeSat Design Specification (CDS)
entries.description: The short standard that created an industry: the mechanical, electrical and operational rules every CubeSat must follow to fit a deployer and fly as a secondary payload.

entries.title: NAR Model Rocket Safety Code
entries.description: The National Association of Rocketry (NAR) code every hobby launch follows: materials, motors, launch distances, recovery. Read before your first launch.

entries.title: Tripoli Unified Safety Code
entries.description: The Tripoli Rocketry Association's safety code for high-power and research rocketry, including certification levels, launch site rules and range safety.

entries.title: 14 CFR Part 101: Amateur Rockets
entries.description: The United States Federal Aviation Administration (FAA) rules in Title 14 of the Code of Federal Regulations (CFR) Part 101: which rockets need airspace waivers, how much notice to give, and operating limits for each class.

entries.title: Rocket Propulsion Elements, 9th ed. (Sutton & Biblarz)
entries.description: The standard rocket-propulsion textbook for over 70 years: thermodynamics of nozzles, liquid and solid engines, feed systems, electric propulsion and testing.

entries.title: Orbital Mechanics for Engineering Students, 4th ed. (Curtis)
entries.description: The friendliest rigorous orbital-mechanics textbook: two-body problem, orbital maneuvers, interplanetary trajectories and attitude dynamics, with MATLAB code for every algorithm.

entries.title: Fundamentals of Astrodynamics, 2nd ed. (Bate, Mueller, White & Saylor)
entries.description: The inexpensive US Air Force Academy classic, updated in 2020: orbit determination, Kepler's problem, ballistic missile trajectories and lunar trajectories in crisp, readable prose.

entries.title: Space Mission Engineering: The New SMAD (Wertz, Everett & Puschell)
entries.description: The 'bible' of space mission design (Space Mission Analysis and Design, SMAD): from mission concept, orbits and payloads through every subsystem to cost and risk, with rules of thumb for sizing everything.

beginner.title: Launch pad
beginner.blurb: No maths required. Build intuition, then build something.

intermediate.blurb: Calculus and physics. Start doing the engineering.

steps.why: Work the two-body problem and orbital maneuvers yourself.
Derive nozzle flow and the rocket equation properly.

channels.name: NASA
channels.why: Launch broadcasts, mission briefings and science explainers straight from the agency.

channels.name: NASA Jet Propulsion Laboratory (JPL)
channels.why: Mars landings, deep-space missions and the 'what's up' night-sky series.

channels.name: NASA Goddard
channels.why: Stunning data visualisations of the Sun, Earth, Moon and Webb from the Scientific Visualization Studio.

channels.name: SpaceX
channels.why: Official launch webcasts with live telemetry: watch Falcon and Starship fly and land.

channels.name: European Space Agency (ESA)
channels.why: Missions, astronauts and Earth observation from Europe's space agency.

channels.name: Everyday Astronaut
channels.why: Tim Dodd's long-form deep dives into engines, rockets and launch-site tours with the engineers.

channels.name: Scott Manley
channels.why: An astrophysicist-programmer explains rocket news, orbital mechanics and failures with real numbers.

channels.name: Smarter Every Day
channels.why: Destin Sandlin's curiosity-driven engineering, including a superb Saturn V series.

channels.name: Veritasium
channels.why: Derek Muller's physics and engineering stories, often with counter-intuitive twists.

channels.name: Kurzgesagt – In a Nutshell
channels.why: Beautifully animated big-picture science: space colonisation, stars, black holes.

channels.name: PBS Space Time
channels.why: Matt O'Dowd's rigorous astrophysics and cosmology, for when you want the real theory.

channels.name: Primal Space
channels.why: Crisp 3D animations of how historic spacecraft and rockets actually worked.

channels.name: Curious Droid
channels.why: Paul Shillito's well-researched histories of space programs and aerospace engineering.

channels.name: Fraser Cain
channels.why: The Universe Today publisher answers space questions and interviews scientists.

videos.title: How did NASA Steer the Saturn V?
videos.why: Gimballed F-1 engines, the Instrument Unit and the guidance loop, explained on real hardware.

videos.title: I Asked an Actual Apollo Engineer to Explain the Saturn 5 Rocket (Long Cut)
videos.why: A full walk-around of a real Saturn V with an engineer who worked on it.

videos.title: The Computer that Controlled the Saturn V
videos.why: Inside the Launch Vehicle Digital Computer and its triple-redundant logic.

videos.title: How the Saturn V Broke into Pieces Launching to the Moon
videos.why: Every staging event, separation and jettison from pad to translunar injection, animated.

videos.title: Rocket Engine Cycles: How Do You Power a Rocket Engine?
videos.why: Pressure-fed, gas-generator, staged and full-flow combustion cycles, compared.

videos.title: How To Do A Hoverslam – Things Kerbal Space Program Doesn't Teach
videos.why: The physics of propulsive landing, the manoeuvre Falcon 9 boosters perform.

videos.title: Rocket Fuel Injectors – Things Kerbal Space Program Doesn't Teach
videos.why: Why injector design makes or breaks a liquid rocket engine.

videos.title: The Bizarre Behavior of Rotating Bodies
videos.why: The intermediate-axis theorem (Dzhanibekov effect) that every attitude engineer must respect.

videos.title: Building a Marsbase is a Horrible Idea: Let's do it!
videos.why: Radiation, dust, gravity and resources: the systems problem of living on Mars.

videos.title: Curiosity's Seven Minutes of Terror
videos.why: JPL engineers explain the sky crane landing before it was attempted.

videos.title: The Deep Space Network: 50 Years of Interplanetary WiFi
videos.why: How three antenna complexes keep every deep-space mission in contact.

videos.title: How Do We Communicate With Faraway Spacecraft?
videos.why: A short classroom-friendly introduction to deep-space radio.

videos.title: Tour of the Moon in 4K
videos.why: Lunar Reconnaissance Orbiter data turned into a narrated flyover of lunar landmarks.

videos.title: Space Debris: Is it a Crisis?
videos.why: ESA's documentary on the growing debris population and what operators must do.

videos.title: Falcon Heavy Test Flight
videos.why: The 2018 debut: two side boosters landing in sync, broadcast with live telemetry.

videos.title: Apollo 11 in Real Time
videos.why: Every minute of the mission's audio, film and transcripts, synchronised. Not a video channel but an unforgettable way to watch.
